Kafka source (dependency-free streaming abstraction)

Source: R/har_online_sources.R
har_source_kafka.Rd

Kafka-shaped source that holds the broker configuration but delegates the actual consumption to a pluggable collector exposing get_next(). Harbinger declares no Kafka dependency: attach a har_simulated_collector() to test end-to-end, or your own collector backed by a real Kafka client (e.g. a reticulate Python consumer) to read a live topic. The collector is pulled one observation at a time, modelling true streaming.

Usage

har_source_kafka(
  topic,
  bootstrap_servers,
  group_id,
  collector = NULL,
  value_schema = NULL,
  name = "kafka"
)

Arguments

topic

Kafka topic name.

bootstrap_servers

Character vector with broker addresses.

group_id

Consumer group identifier.

collector

Optional collector object exposing get_next() (and an optional close()). Without one the source raises on next_observation().

value_schema

Optional schema description for the payload.

name

Source name.

Value

A har_source_kafka object.

Examples

# Stub example: a simulated collector, no broker required.
source <- har_source_kafka(
  topic = "sensor-events",
  bootstrap_servers = c("broker:9092"),
  group_id = "harbinger",
  collector = har_simulated_collector(c(10, 11, 12, 20, 12))
)
next_observation(source)$observation$value
#> [1] 10

# Real example: a collector backed by a live Kafka client (user code).
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
kafka_collector <- function(consumer) {
  obj <- list(
    get_next = function() {
      msg <- reticulate::iter_next(consumer, completed = NULL)
      if (is.null(msg)) NULL else as.numeric(msg$value)
    },
    close = function() consumer$close()
  )
  class(obj) <- append("kafka_collector", "har_stream_collector")
  obj
}
# consumer <- reticulate::import("kafka")$KafkaConsumer("sensor-events", ...)
# source <- har_source_kafka("sensor-events", c("broker:9092"), "harbinger",
#                            collector = kafka_collector(consumer))
} # }
